gap: No result ChatGPT got lines up the 24 V split-phase models side by side at today's prices: Sigineer's APC6024D costs $949 on sigineer.com. That is $271 less than the $1,220 Sun Gold 6000W 24V that ChatGPT called 'best overall value', and $867 less than AIMS's 6000 W 24 V unit at $1,816 ($2,115 for the UL/CSA-listed SKU). The $936 Sun Gold 4000W 24V saves only $13 over the 6,000 W Sigineer.
standout_why: Compared against the cited Sigineer APC6024D page, the ecosolarkits.com split-phase guide (2026-11-11) and our own dealectric.com/best-split-phase-inverter (2026-11-10). The Sigineer page shows only its own price ($949), its own 3,000 W per-leg cap and its 80 W idle draw. Eco Solar Kits lists only 48 V models and says its '24V split-phase models are sold out'. Our page has no 24 V model at all. None of them prices Sun Gold, AIMS and Sigineer 24 V units against each other, and ChatGPT's answer ranked Sun Gold as best value without that comparison.
decides: This changes the value pick. At the 6,000 W tier, the Sigineer APC6024D at $949 is the cheapest 24 V native split-phase inverter-charger whose price I opened. It undercuts both the Sun Gold 6000W 24V ($1,220) and the Sun Gold 4000W 24V ($936 buys 2,000 W less for $13 less). AIMS keeps the 'documented certification' slot, but only the PICOGLF6024240SUL SKU at $2,115; the non-UL PICOGLF60W24V240VS is $1,816. Whoever buys the Sigineer should know it caps each 120 V leg at 3,000 W and idles at 80 W (15 W in power-saver mode).
